tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized using enacted tax rates for the estimated future tax effects of temporary differences between the book and tax basis of recorded assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance if it is more likely than not that some portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. At December 31, 2025, the Company had deferred tax liabilities in excess of deferred tax assets of approximately $130 million.

The Company evaluates all tax positions taken on the federal and state tax filings to determine if the position is more likely than not to be sustained upon examination. For positions that meet the more likely than not to be sustained criteria, an evaluation to determine the largest amount of benefit, determined on a cumulative probability basis, that is more likely than not to be realized upon ultimate settlement is determined. A previously recognized tax position is reversed when it is subsequently determined that a tax position no longer meets the more likely than not threshold to be sustained. The evaluation of the sustainability of a tax position and the probable amount that is more likely than not is based on judgment, historical experience and on various other assumptions that the Company believes are reasonable under the circumstances.

In June 2026, the majority partner announced a key piece of equipment, a stacker reclaimer machine, at DTA sustained significant damage due to high winds from a storm. DTA leadership, as part of DTA’s insurance claims process, is in contact with its insurance providers to evaluate its options and work on developing an action plan. intro.text: We are a world-class producer and exporter of high-quality, low-cost coals, including metallurgical and thermal coals. We play an essential role in meeting the world’s growing need for energy, steel, cement and other infrastructure solutions. Our products have global access due to our ownership interests in two marine export terminals and access to several other third-party owned terminals. lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 37% of our coal revenue was from U.S. electric power generators, 56% was from export markets, comprising 8%, 20% and 28% from power generators, industrial and metallurgical customers, respectively, and 7% was from other domestic customers.

During the year ended December 31, 2024, approximately 31% of our coal revenue was from U.S. electric power generators, 66% was from export markets, comprising 12%, 35% and 19% from power generators, industrial and metallurgical customers, respectively, and 3% was from other domestic customers.

During the year ended December 31, 2023, approximately 27% of our coal revenue was from U.S. electric power generators, 71% was from export markets, comprising 16%, 40% and 15% from power generators, industrial and metallurgical customers, respectively, and 2% was from other domestic customers.
During the year ended December 31, 2024, two customers each comprised over 10% of our total sales, aggregating approximately 22% of our total sales.

For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, approximately 56%, 66% and 71%, respectively, of our annual coal revenue was derived from customers who exported our coal outside of the U.S., and we expect that international sales will continue to account for a large portion of our revenue as we seek international expansion opportunities.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, approximately 56 %, 66 % and 71 %, respectively, of the Company’s coal revenues were derived from exports.
